aving laid the conceptual foundation for relating properties of solids to chemical bonding in Chapter 21, we turn now to applications of these concepts to three important classes of ma te rials: ceramics, electronic ma te rials, and optical ma te rials. All of these are synthetic ma te rials fashioned from inorganic, nonmetallic substances by chemical methods of synthesis and processing.

Ceramics are one of the oldest classes of ma te rials prepared by humankind. New discoveries in ceramics are occurring at a startling rate, and major new tech- nologic advances will certainly come from these discoveries. Ceramics have value both as structural ma te rials— the role emphasized in this chapter— and for their wide range of electronic and optical properties.
